known_info.kb_body:
E-Commerce Website Service Restoration Procedure
Document Version: 1.0 | Effective Date: December 2025
Author: Joanne Simpson (USER_004)
The E-Commerce Website service (SVC_007) is a business-critical service that depends on the primary database server (CI_001) for transaction processing and data availability, along with redundant web application servers to ensure continuous access.
During the database upgrade, the environment was enhanced to improve stability and reliability, the database server serial number was updated to DB-2025-PROD-001, and post-upgrade validation confirmed data integrity and system readiness.
For database-related service disruptions, restoration involves validating database availability, confirming application connectivity, reviewing system logs, verifying dependent configuration items, and assessing performance indicators. If required, a controlled failover to a standby database is performed following approved recovery procedures.
Restoration activities included system validation, database migration and optimization, CMDB updates, service status restoration, and stakeholder notification. Preventive measures include automated health monitoring, periodic capacity reviews, maintained recovery runbooks, scheduled failover drills, and proactive hardware lifecycle management.
Escalations are handled by the service owner (User_001) and the Infrastructure Team, with 24/7 support available at servicedesk@techcorp.com.

If asked whether to register a new CI or update the existing record, say update the serial on the existing record. If asked whether the service is restored, say yes, mark it operational. isolated.detail: Raising PRB_009's impact to high also raises the linked incident INC_061 (ORG_013) from moderate to high priority. Policy §6 REQUIRES 'Incident priority changes -> reset/swap/cancel the incident_sla row per the change'. INC_061 has no incident_sla row. In the MSP seed, client incidents use the provider's (ORG_001) SLA definitions (e.g. INC_049 in ORG_013 carries SLA_002), so two readings are defensible: do nothing because there is no row to reset, or start an SLA for the new priority, where high has two ORG_001 definitions (SLA_003 response, SLA_004 resolution). Full-DB scoring would give one reasonable behaviour 0. Releasing it needs a fixed MSP SLA rule, which the user declined to set (D6D-1). The 6D-1 screening's statement that ORG_013 'has no SLA definition, so no SLA action' was wrong and is corrected.

Recording SRV-LNX-4421, the point of the task, is therefore not enforced by the training reward. Not fixed by re-wording the operator's text after the failure (that would tune the task to the scorer); any redesign needs the user's decision.

Open incidents of the 'Level 1 Support Team' created before 20 February 2024 should be treated with top-priority attention. You want an alert sent to each user those incidents are currently assigned to, with your subject and message template (incident number, summary and creation date filled in). The incidents themselves are not edited.

Give the subject and the message template from known_info when asked, and explain the fields. If the agent asks whether to change the incidents' priority or other fields, say no, only send the alerts. Confirm the agent's plan otherwise. End once the alerts are sent.
